physics:
### Build a numerical checklist, not just a formula sheet

For each retained numerical problem, write the known quantities, the unknown quantity and the physical relationship linking them. Convert units before substitution and keep the unit with the final answer. Then explain whether the result is physically plausible. This separates a calculation you understand from one whose answer you memorised.

A deletion in a measurement subsection does not make all measurement skills irrelevant. A retained force or energy question may still require units and interpretation. Learn the prerequisites needed to solve retained work, while keeping the officially excluded assessment references distinct. Your teacher can help with a prerequisite that is no longer directly assessed.

### Keep conceptual and calculation practice separate

Use one notebook column for why a relationship holds and another for how to calculate with it. Draw the physical situation before choosing an equation. If your result has the wrong sign, revisit the chosen direction; if its size is unreasonable, revisit conversion and substitution. These checks are useful even when the final answer happens to match.

When practising a retained explanation, answer the actual command: define, distinguish, explain or derive. A definition alone is not a derivation. For diagrams, label quantities consistently with your written working. Choose practice from retained material only after checking all columns of the ALP table.

### Review mistakes by cause

Record whether each mistake came from a wrong concept, wrong equation, algebra, units or incomplete explanation. Redo the question without looking at the correction. On a later day, attempt a similar retained question with different values. The aim is to reproduce the reasoning, not the appearance of a solved example.
chemistry:
### Separate topic deletions from exercise deletions

Chemistry tables often place several question categories in one row. Build a small checklist with columns for topic, MCQ, short answer, descriptive answer and numerical problem. Copy only the references that actually appear. This prevents the common mistake of crossing out a whole unit because one question category has several exclusions.

For retained calculations, begin with the chemical meaning before choosing an arithmetic operation. Identify the quantities given, write the relevant relationship and show units. Where an equation is needed, check its balance. A correct-looking number obtained from an unbalanced relationship is not a dependable method.

### Learn explanations through comparisons

For a retained comparison, choose a small set of consistent features rather than writing unrelated sentences on each side. When explaining a trend, state the trend and then the reason. When discussing a particle model, connect the model to the observed property. Avoid copying an attractive diagram without knowing what each feature represents.

Do not reuse a remembered exercise number from another edition. Read the question wording and compare its page reference with the ALP. This matters especially when a deletion covers only part of a subsection or a named numerical problem. Keep an older tuition handout separate from the current verified list until reconciled.

### Practise an answer from a blank page

Close the textbook and write the explanation, equation or worked solution from memory. Open the book only to check missing steps. Mark errors such as an incorrect charge, symbol, coefficient or condition, then rewrite the answer correctly. Use retained question types from the official model paper to check presentation under time pressure.
mathematics:
### Make the exercise number part of every practice entry

A Mathematics ALP can exclude one example, several subparts, a complete exercise or selected review questions. Record all four levels: unit, exercise, question and subpart. A note saying chapter reduced is too vague to guide tomorrow's practice. Use a tick beside retained questions and a separate mark beside the exclusions.

Start a retained problem by identifying what is given and what must be shown or calculated. Write the transformation that moves you towards the target, then justify each operation. In algebra, signs, brackets and restrictions matter as much as the final line. Where a value can be substituted back into the original relationship, use that as a check.

### Avoid learning only one worked example

After studying a method, close the solution and solve a retained question without prompts. Then try another question with changed values or a different arrangement. If you cannot start, identify the missing idea rather than copying the whole solution again. Keep a short error log for sign changes, formula selection and omitted working.

A topic omitted from direct examination may still supply background needed for a retained method. Ask your teacher about a prerequisite rather than assuming that a deleted heading removes every later dependency. Examination scope and mathematical understanding are related, but they are not identical lists.

### Use the model paper as a timing exercise

Read the available choices before beginning, number answers clearly and reserve time to inspect arithmetic and omitted subparts. Do not infer guaranteed future questions from the model paper. Use its structure to practise selecting questions you can complete accurately within the stated time.
biology:
### Turn retained material into connected explanations

Biology is easier to revise when a term is attached to a function, structure or sequence. For each retained heading, explain what it describes, how it works and why it matters in the surrounding chapter. A list of memorised terms is less useful when a question changes its wording or asks for a comparison.

For a retained diagram, practise drawing it from a blank page, then add the labels without looking. Check which features distinguish it from a similar structure. Do not automatically delete a whole page because one figure, table or box is named in the ALP. Locate the exact referenced item before marking your book.

### Keep exercise categories separate

A row can exclude named short answers but all inquisitive questions. These are different instructions. Use separate checklist columns so that an all label does not spread to unrelated categories. Match chapter names and page numbers whenever the source uses a generic label such as table or key points.

For a retained comparison, use the same criteria on both sides. For a process, explain the stages in sequence and connect each stage to its outcome. For a definition, use the necessary identifying features. This produces concise, complete answers without adding unrelated paragraphs merely to make the page look full.

### Test recall before rereading

After a revision block, close the book and answer three retained prompts. Check the missing scientific terms and incomplete links in your explanation. Revisit those weaknesses on a later day. When using the model paper, treat it as an assessment-format example, not a prediction that only those exact questions can appear.
english:
### Keep comprehension, vocabulary and writing in your plan

Removing textbook units does not remove every English skill. Begin by listing the retained units and the separate language/composition tasks described in the paper instructions. For each retained text, write a short outline of its main idea, the supporting details and the author's purpose. Practise answering the question asked rather than reproducing a memorised paragraph.

Study vocabulary in context. Write a sentence using a retained word, then explain how its meaning changes the sentence. For verb-form practice, identify the time and structure signalled by the sentence before selecting an answer. Reading the surrounding words is more reliable than choosing the option that merely sounds familiar.

### Practise writing with the stated format

For a composition task included in the official instructions, plan the opening, development and closing before writing. Keep the purpose and audience clear. After finishing, check sentence boundaries, tense consistency, spelling and whether every required point has been answered. A well-organised answer is easier to review than a long answer with no clear structure.

For poetry that remains in your syllabus, distinguish the literal situation from the idea or feeling it develops. Support an explanation with relevant detail from the retained text. Do not transfer a deleted unit's prepared answer into a different question simply because a few words overlap.

### Use unit groups accurately

When the paper instructions identify different unit groups, prepare each group rather than selecting only the shortest texts. Read the number of questions offered and the number required. During a timed attempt, number answers clearly and reserve time to proofread. The subject PDF, not an old grammar handout, controls the current allocation.
urdu:
### Maintain separate lists for prose, poetry and composition

Urdu preparation becomes clearer when literary selections are separated from language and writing tasks. Copy the excluded titles and their textbook page ranges into a short checklist. Then build a retained-selection list from your own edition. Do not rely on a transliterated title alone: the original Urdu heading and author identify the intended selection more reliably.

For retained prose, explain the central idea in your own words, identify supporting details and practise the prescribed question types. For retained poetry, distinguish the literal wording, context and intended meaning. Avoid using a prepared explanation whose opening lines belong to a different poem or ghazal.

### Preserve the difference between exclusion and choice

A selection excluded by the official notice is outside the indicated scope. A question offered with choice in the paper is a different matter. Do not treat optional answering choices as permission to ignore an entire retained category. Read the full paper instructions before deciding how much time to allocate to prose, poetry and composition.

Practise writing, not only oral recall. Check spelling, agreement, sentence clarity and whether the answer addresses the command. If a prescribed format is included, practise its layout as well as its content. A familiar topic can still lose clarity when the answer has no structure or changes its purpose halfway through.

### Review with the textbook open only after attempting

Write a retained explanation from memory, then compare it with the text and your teacher's notes. Correct a missing idea rather than extending the answer with unrelated sentences. Use the original subject PDF to settle a page/title mismatch and ask your teacher when your textbook edition differs.
islamiat:
### Match original names and numbered references carefully

An Islamiat exclusion list may identify a Hadith number, a particular theme or named biographical material. Preserve that level of detail when marking the textbook. A list of selected personalities does not automatically delete every personality in the chapter. Where numbering or spelling differs in your edition, ask your teacher before changing the scope of preparation.

For retained material, connect the central teaching with its explanation and practical meaning. Separate a definition from a longer discussion and keep the answer relevant to the question. Learn prescribed references accurately from the approved textbook instead of relying on an unattributed quotation circulating on social media.

### Prepare recall and understanding together

After reading a retained section, close the book and state its main teaching. Then explain it in complete sentences and give an appropriate example where the question requires one. Reopen the book to check accuracy. Avoid inventing an attribution or wording when you cannot remember it precisely.

Use separate checklist entries for Hadith, themes and biographical material. This makes partial exclusions visible and helps prevent an entire chapter being crossed out because one row contains several names. Keep the official source beside tuition notes until the references have been reconciled.

### Resolve document conflicts before a final plan

The correct response to inconsistent dates or wording is clarification, not a guess. Show the original page and the covering notification to your teacher or board. Keep a record of any later corrected notice. A website summary is useful for navigation and preparation, but it cannot overrule a corrected official instruction or establish that a conflicting note has been formally withdrawn.
computer-science:
### Use the retained unit as the boundary of each exercise

Read the topic and exercise columns separately before choosing coding or theory practice. In this subject, software development, Python, algorithms, data work, ethics and entrepreneurship are different areas. A deleted Python subsection should not be treated as deletion of the whole programming unit, and a fully retained unit deserves the same attention as one with a long exclusion row.

For retained code, predict the output before running it. Track variable values line by line, explain why a condition is true or false, and identify which statement changes the state. Then run the example and compare the result. If it differs, locate the first point where your prediction and execution disagree.

### Prepare theory with concrete examples

For a retained algorithm question, explain the input, processing steps and expected output. For a digital-literacy or ethical question, describe a realistic situation and connect it to the principle being tested. Do not replace an explanation with a list of technical words. In entrepreneurship material, distinguish the idea, the user's need and the practical decision being discussed.

The ALP marks some units as fully retained. Add those units explicitly to your revision checklist instead of focusing only on what was removed. The official exercise references also matter: a deleted long question is not evidence that every short question on the same broad subject has disappeared.

### Keep the written-paper format in view

Use the model paper to practise concise definitions, complete short answers and longer explanations at the stated time allocation. Practical coding helps understanding, but a written examination still requires clear explanation on paper. Treat the model as an example of structure and level, not a promise of exact future questions.
